name: Meta Platforms
basis: each funding- or dividend-inclusive history is scaled to its own latest raw USD close

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded
onchainSpot.liquiditySource: direct CEX order books; direct Ethereum, Robinhood-chain, and PancakeSwap V3 quoter depth; direct Meteora pool state; and direct Jupiter executable round-trip quotes

peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: GOOGL 37.9% with 3/3 replicate support; XYZ100 19.0% with 3/3 replicate support; AMZN 17.2% with 3/3 replicate support; NVDA 15.5% with 3/3 replicate support; MSFT 10.3% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet is the closest direct substitute: Search and YouTube compete for the same digital advertising budgets and consumer attention as Meta's Facebook and Instagram, and both companies are spending heavily on AI models and data centers.

peers.name: Nasdaq-100
peers.reason: The primary hedge also belongs in the peer basket because the Nasdaq-100 carries a large share of Meta's return variance: Meta is a top index constituent and the index aggregates the same mega-cap platform and AI-infrastructure complex that drives Meta's systematic moves.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon competes for digital advertising budgets through retail media and sponsored listings and shares the AI and cloud data-center capital spending cycle, making it a close economic comparator though less direct than Alphabet.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is a key supplier of AI accelerators and Meta is a major customer, so NVIDIA captures the shared input cost and AI infrastructure cycle that drives Meta's capital spending and product roadmap; the directly traded equity is preferred over wrapper or leveraged proxies.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is a fellow mega-cap platform company whose returns are driven by the same forces that matter for Meta: enterprise and consumer software monetization, cloud and AI capital expenditure cycles, and sensitivity to the same long-duration mega-cap discount-rate moves. It is a direct competitor in AI and a close comparator on scale, margins, and capex intensity.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Meta Platforms is a top-weighted mega-cap constituent of the Nasdaq-100, so the Nasdaq-100 is the cleanest traded instrument for absorbing the generic systematic and mega-cap growth co-movement that should not be attributed to individual peers. It is also the most liquid index in the universe at 112.11 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity, well above Meta's own 4.965 USD millions, which makes it practical as the primary hedge for generic systematic risk.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
